newsitem.title: FRANCE: IMI Sigeco cuts Peugeot forecast, turns seller.
newsitem.headline: IMI Sigeco cuts Peugeot forecast, turns seller.

text.p: IMI Sigeco has cut 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for French carmaker PSA Peugeot Citroen.
In a note to investors IMI Sigeco analyst Sabine Blumel said on Friday that she had changed her recommendation on the group to sell from hold, saying the stock was overvalued.

"On the basis that Peugeot was barely profitable in the second half of 1996 and that it seems less well-equipped to operate successfully in the current European market environment than we expected, we have severely cut our earnings estimates for 1997 and 1998," the report said.
On April 17 Peugeot said profits fell by more than half in 1996 to 734 million francs as a fierce price war raged in the French car market.

Blumel said she expected Peugeot's profitability to continue to decline and the group to report a net loss of three francs per share in 1997 against a previous estimate of a profit of 24 francs per share.

She said this assumed the price war in France and in southern Europe would intensify in 1997 and the group's market share continues to decline in a contracting French and a lacklustre West European market.
For 1998 the analyst said the group's profitability might improve slightly as sales volume should grow due to a recovery of the French market.
But she cut her EPS forecast for 1998 to a profit of 16 francs from a previous target of 42 francs.
Peugeot shares were down 2.13 percent to 598 francs at 1000 GMT on the Paris bourse.
